flux2-klein-mflux.licence: Apache-2.0 per the Hugging Face model card (black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B), commercial use allowed, not gated; the 9B klein is non-commercial. Read 2026-11-12.
flux2-klein-mflux.quality: All three reference images match their briefs closely (grey streak, yellow jacket, wet planks and pink sky); photographic, clean faces and hands, no text artefacts.
flux2-klein-mflux.notes: 1024x1024, 4 steps (default), 4-bit: 26 s per image cold and warm (about 5.7 s per step), peak memory footprint 12.5 GB (resident 9.0 GB; MLX reports 9.3 GB). Outputs are Apache-2.0, so the 768 px copies are committed in spikes/draft-final/inputs/.

kokoro-mlx.licence: Apache-2.0 per the model cards of hexgrad/Kokoro-82M and mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16, not gated. Read 2026-11-12.
kokoro-mlx.quality: Audible and clean (mean -25 to -27 dB, peaks -6 to -9 dB; no silent/NaN output on M4 Pro). Not listened to by a human yet. A Whisper large-v3-turbo transcription of both files reproduces the text exactly (only homophone spellings Mariah and key/quay differ), so the words and the English are right.
kokoro-mlx.notes: mlx-audio 0.6.5 + misaki[en]. Line "Is anyone there?" (1.7 s, af_heart, US English): 3 s including model load, peak footprint 1.8 GB. Narration (24.3 s of audio, bm_george, British English): 3 s, peak footprint 6.8 GB (resident 0.8 GB), so about 8x faster than real time even with loading. One recorded run says no-output: that was a wrong --out name (--join_audio drops the _000 suffix), not a failure.

musicgen.licence: Weights facebook/musicgen-small: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial) per the Hugging Face model card, not gated; audiocraft code MIT. Read 2026-11-12. Fine for testing; not usable for a free app whose users may sell their films. Output audio not committed.
musicgen.quality: 30.0 s WAV at 32 kHz, mean -18.5 dB, peak -3.5 dB, no silent stretch over 1 s. Not listened to by a human yet: UNVERIFIED whether it sounds like the prompt (acoustic guitar and cello folk).
musicgen.notes: musicgen-small (300M) through transformers 5.22.2 on PyTorch 2.15 MPS (audiocraft pins torch 2.1, which has no Python 3.12 wheels). 82 s wall for 30 s of audio, of which 26 s generation and the rest Python and model load, peak footprint 5.9 GB. Runner: spikes/mac/scripts/musicgen.py.

ltx23-ltx2mlx-q4.licence: LTX-2 Community License, accepted by use: free for entities under USD 10M annual revenue, paid licence above; no region limits beyond a sanctions representation; outputs belong to the user; acceptable-use policy requires disclosing machine-generated content when published. Read 2026-11-12; the human approved use and the download. Text encoder mlx-community/gemma-3-12b-it-4bit: Gemma Terms of Use (prohibited-use policy, no region limits), not gated.
ltx23-ltx2mlx-q4.quality: All ten shots rendered, text only (no reference images). Composition and camera moves are good: locked-off harbour (S01), real pan (S03), steady tracking shot (S08, best), over-the-shoulder (S09), rising wide (S10); push-in in S02 barely visible. Generated audio is in sync and S05 says the line: a Whisper transcription of the audio track reads exactly "Is anyone there?". Faces and hands clean at 832x448. Weak points: identity is not controlled by text (Maria became a man in S04, Tom a young man in a suit in S09, hair colour changes in S08), S06 drifts from the hands to a face, S07 is not locked-off (a door moves), rain barely visible (S01, S09). 4 s holds together; no melting seen. Judged from sampled frames by the agent; not yet watched by a human.
ltx23-ltx2mlx-q4.notes: ltx-2-mlx 0.18.0, distilled two-stage (8 steps at half resolution, x2 latent upscale, 3 refine steps), int4 transformer, 832x480 requested and rounded to 832x448, 97 frames at 24 fps, seed 1. Steady speed 167-169 s per 4 s clip (S01 cold and warm, S02, S05, S09, S10): about 7.2 s per stage-1 step and 29 s per stage-2 step; cold and warm are the same, so loading is a small share. S03, S04, S06, S07 and S08 took 189-202 s: the GPU ran 18-23 % slower per step during that stretch, which partly overlapped a 12 GB download; cause of the rest UNVERIFIED (no thermal warning recorded). Peak memory footprint 15-18 GiB; the tool itself reports 18.5 GB peak Metal memory during VAE decode, so the footprint figure still undercounts slightly. An earlier S01 attempt froze when the Mac slept on battery (log ltx23-q4-S01-aborted-sleep.log); all runs since use caffeinate -i.

wan22-5b-comfyui-gguf.licence: Apache-2.0 on Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, QuantStack/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B-GGUF and Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged; text encoder city96/umt5-xxl-encoder-gguf Apache-2.0 (UMT5 by Google). None gated. Read 2026-11-14. ComfyUI itself is GPL-3.0: run as a separate program only, nothing copied into this repository.
wan22-5b-comfyui-gguf.quality: All ten shots rendered, text only, no audio (the model has none). Clean, detailed pictures at 832x480, but it mostly ignores camera directions: S02 has no push-in, S03 no pan, S10 no rising drift (a ferry at sea, no harbour); S01 and S07 are correctly locked-off (S07 kettle, porthole and steam are good). Less motion overall than LTX. Faces: S05 is a good close-up but the last second cuts to black. S04 shows both people from behind (direction asked for faces), Tom in a suit. S08 walks away down a corridor but the hood changes from dark to blue and it is not a ship. S09 came out as a cartoon of the wrong character: style is not stable from text alone. S06 hands and rope are partly deformed. Identity is not controlled, as with LTX. Judged from sampled frames by the agent; not yet watched by a human.
wan22-5b-comfyui-gguf.notes: ComfyUI eee5918 + ComfyUI-GGUF 6ea2651 on PyTorch 2.15 MPS. Q8_0 GGUF transformer, UMT5-XXL Q8_0 text encoder (on the CPU), 832x480, 97 frames at 24 fps, 20 steps uni_pc, cfg 5, shift 8, seed 1. 1234-1267 s per 4 s clip (about 48 s per sampling step plus loading and VAE decode), so about 7.4x slower than LTX int4; times were steady across all ten. Peak memory footprint 27.7-29.7 GiB. S02 and S05 shared the GPU with short F5-TTS runs (under 30 s each), which did not change their times noticeably. A VS Code crash stopped the first chain during S06; S06-S10 were re-run from scratch.

wan21-1.3b-comfyui.blockers: Too slow on this Mac for its quality: one 4 s clip at its native 832x480 takes about an hour. Only S01 was rendered; the other nine were not, as they cannot change the verdict.
wan21-1.3b-comfyui.licence: Apache-2.0 on Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B and Comfy-Org/Wan_2.1_ComfyUI_repackaged, not gated. Read 2026-11-14.
wan21-1.3b-comfyui.quality: S01 (static night harbour): right composition and a locked-off camera, but the wet quay is blown out to white glare, the lamps are white instead of yellow and no rain is visible. Clearly below Wan 2.2 5B and LTX 2.3 on the same shot. 832x480, 65 frames at 16 fps, no audio. Judged from sampled frames by the agent.
wan21-1.3b-comfyui.notes: ComfyUI as for wan22-5b-comfyui-gguf, fp16 weights, 30 steps uni_pc, cfg 6, shift 8, seed 1. 3564 s in total, 115 s per sampling step, peak memory footprint 33.8 GB: slower and bigger than Wan 2.2 5B because the Wan 2.1 VAE compresses 8x8 instead of 16x16, so the transformer sees about 2.7x as many tokens. A first attempt ran at 161 s per step and passed the 45 min limit; the driver then left ComfyUI running after bench stopped it (fixed: the server now shares the driver's process group), so that attempt has no record. The full-size rerun used a 120 min limit with the human's approval.

wan22-mlx.blockers: mlx-video needs the original Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B weights (31.9 GB, over the 20 GB ask-first limit) converted to MLX, and installs from a git checkout (human-run). The same model already runs in ComfyUI (wan22-5b-comfyui-gguf), so the remaining question is only runtime speed.
wan22-mlx.licence: Apache-2.0 (Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B model card, not gated), read 2026-11-14.

hunyuanvideo15-comfyui.blockers: Time: Wan 2.2 5B, a smaller model, already takes about 21 min per 4 s clip in ComfyUI on this Mac; HunyuanVideo 1.5 (8.3B) would be slower still. Not attempted so the session could go to plan 10b.

ltx2-comfyui-mps.blockers: Optional by design: only needed if the MLX route failed, and LTX-2.3 runs on MLX (ltx23-ltx2mlx-q4).

minimax-h3-gguf.licence: MiniMax H3 Community License, read and approved by the human on 2026-11-15 (they are not in the EU, which the licence Q&A excludes). Not gated. Weights: unsloth/MiniMax-H3-GGUF (Q8_0 transformers, Q4_K_M Qwen3-VL text encoder) plus Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 VAEs and turbo LoRAs. Runtime stable-diffusion.cpp is MIT. Clips are not committed; they travel in the rating package only.
minimax-h3-gguf.quality: Checked 2026-11-15 on stills at 2.5 s (17 turbo clips): clearly the best pictures of the spike, cinematic lighting and believable people. Text-only (t2v) invents a new person each shot, like every other model. With reference images (r2v, Ref2VA) Maria and Tom keep face, hair and clothes across all seven shots, two characters per shot included (S04, S09): the first local model that solves recurring characters. Every clip has an audio track (ambience, sound effects), but loudness varies from -11 to -55 dB mean, so it needs normalising. One r2v clip (S04) put a real brand logo (The North Face) on Tom's jacket. Human rating pending. Full 20-step runs (S02, S05, S08, t2v and r2v) keep the same framing as turbo with slightly finer detail and a colder grade; on stills not worth about 3x the time.
minimax-h3-gguf.notes: stable-diffusion.cpp built from source with Metal; ComfyUI-GGUF cannot read unsloth's text encoder. 832x480, 107 frames (4.46 s), 24 fps. Turbo LoRA: t2v 6 steps 985-998 s per clip (about 140 s per step, plus about 120 s video decode), r2v 4 steps 888-1099 s. Peak footprint 22.3-22.5 GB with --params-backend disk --mmap (--offload-to-cpu is killed for doubling memory on unified memory). About 6x slower than LTX 2.3 per clip. Disk: about 69 GB of weights. Full 20 steps without LoRA: t2v 2829-2841 s, r2v 3203-3205 s, peak 20.8-21.0 GB.

f5tts-mlx.licence: Code: f5-tts-mlx 0.2.6 (lucasnewman/f5-tts-mlx) is MIT. Weights: the MLX conversion lucasnewman/f5-tts-mlx is tagged MIT on Hugging Face, but it converts SWivid/F5-TTS, whose weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (trained on Emilia), so treat them as non-commercial. Not gated. Read 2026-11-14. Outputs clone the human's voice and stay on this Mac; none are committed.
f5tts-mlx.quality: Clones the human's own voice from a 5.8 s reference (their recording, trimmed, loudness-normalised to -20 LUFS, 24 kHz mono). Whisper large-v3-turbo transcribes both cloned lines exactly ("Is anyone there?", "We should go back to the cabin before the rain gets worse."). The model's own duration guess is too fast (0.65 s and 2.0 s); with explicit durations (1.4 s and 3.4 s of new speech) the pace is natural. Listened to on 2026-11-14: the human thinks it sounds like them; someone who knows their voice well hears audible differences. Recognisable, not indistinguishable.
f5tts-mlx.notes: f5-tts-mlx 0.2.6 fails with mlx 0.32 (TypeError in mx.random.normal); pinning mlx<0.23 (0.22.1) fixes it. --duration counts the reference audio too, so it must be reference length plus new speech (7.2 s and 9.2 s here); 1.4 s gave noise that Whisper heard as "Thank you.". 17-26 s per line including model load, peak footprint 2.2-2.6 GB. All F5 runs shared the GPU with a Wan 2.2 render, so the times are pessimistic. The first two recorded failures are the mlx version error.

ace-step-mlx.blockers: No PyPI route: the listed mlx-serve is an unrelated LLM server, mlx-audio's music generator only supports MiniMax Music 3, and ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT per its Hugging Face card) installs from its git repository, which needs a human-run install.
ace-step-mlx.licence: ACE-Step/Ace-Step1.5: MIT per the Hugging Face card, not gated (read 2026-11-12).

summary: Recommended local defaults on an M4 Pro 48 GB (measured 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-14): video LTX 2.3 distilled int4 through ltx-2-mlx, image FLUX.2 klein 4B through mflux, speech Kokoro 82M through mlx-audio, music MusicGen small (non-commercial weights; ACE-Step not tried yet). LTX is the only video model fast enough for a queue: about 2.8 min per 4 s clip at 832x448 with in-sync audio, against about 21 min for Wan 2.2 5B (no audio, ignores camera directions) and about an hour for Wan 2.1 1.3B (worst pictures). No local video model keeps a character's identity from text alone, so recurring characters need reference conditioning (plan 10b). Voice cloning works locally with F5-TTS but its weights are non-commercial.
